about: Test vectors for the normalisation contract. Ingestion runs in Python and verification runs in Go, so the two cannot share a function; what they share is this file. Both suites read it and both must agree, because drift between them surfaces as quote-match failures on visually identical text, which is miserable to diagnose from the symptom. Fingerprints are hashes of post-normalisation text, so changing the contract invalidates every fingerprint file and forces a re-bless of every corpus: bump normalisation_version when that happens, and make it deliberate.
text_provenance: Every string here is invented. No corpus text enters this repository, from any source, whatever its licence (ADR-0014).

vectors.name: step0-removes-ufeff
vectors.why: U+FEFF (byte order mark) is invisible and is whitespace in neither standard library, so it survives every later step and produces a quote mismatch on text that looks identical

vectors.name: step0-removes-u200b
vectors.why: U+200B (zero width space) is invisible and is whitespace in neither standard library, so it survives every later step and produces a quote mismatch on text that looks identical

vectors.name: step0-removes-u200c
vectors.why: U+200C (zero width non-joiner) is invisible and is whitespace in neither standard library, so it survives every later step and produces a quote mismatch on text that looks identical

vectors.name: step0-removes-u200d

vectors.name: step0-removes-u00ad

vectors.name: step0-removes-rather-than-replaces
vectors.why: a removed format character leaves nothing behind; treating it as whitespace would insert a space that is not in the source

vectors.name: step0-runs-before-nfc-so-composition-still-happens
vectors.why: the zero width joiner sits between the base letter and its combining acute. Stripping first lets NFC compose; normalising first leaves the sequence decomposed and the strip cannot undo it. This is what fixes the step order

vectors.name: step0-list-is-closed-mongolian-vowel-separator-survives
vectors.why: U+180E is a format character and was White_Space before Unicode 6.3, so an implementation reaching for a category test rather than the named list will drop or collapse it. The contract names five characters and this is not one

vectors.name: step1-nfc-composes-combining-acute
vectors.why: the same word arrives decomposed from one extractor and composed from another; NFC is what makes the two hash alike

vectors.name: step1-nfc-composes-angstrom-sign
vectors.why: U+212B ANGSTROM SIGN has a canonical decomposition, so NFC maps it onto U+00C5 — a singleton substitution rather than a composition

vectors.name: step1-nfc-reorders-combining-marks-canonically
vectors.why: neither mark composes with q, so the only thing NFC does here is canonical ordering: combining class 220 sorts before 230. An implementation that composes without reordering passes every other vector in this file

vectors.name: step1-nfc-is-idempotent
vectors.why: already-composed text is unchanged, so re-normalising a stored chunk cannot invalidate its fingerprint

vectors.name: step1-is-nfc-not-nfkc-ligature-survives
vectors.why: NFKC would expand the fi ligature to two letters. That is a different text, and a quote taken from the source would then fail to match it

vectors.name: step1-is-nfc-not-nfkc-fullwidth-survives
vectors.why: NFKC would fold fullwidth forms to ASCII. Same reason: compatibility normalisation rewrites the text rather than canonicalising it

vectors.name: step2-collapses-u0009

vectors.name: step2-collapses-crlf
vectors.why: a line break is one run, not two: CRLF collapses to a single space, so the same paragraph hashes alike whichever line ending the extractor emitted

vectors.name: step2-collapses-a-mixed-run
vectors.why: a run is a run whatever it is made of; the replacement is always one U+0020

vectors.name: step2-leaves-u001c-alone
vectors.why: U+001C is matched by Python's \s and by str.isspace, and is not matched by Go's unicode.IsSpace. It does not have the White_Space property, so the contract preserves it — this is the exact vector 'collapse whitespace' alone would have left as two different functions

vectors.name: step3-trims-both-ends
vectors.why: leading and trailing whitespace is dropped after collapsing, not before

vectors.name: step3-trims-non-ascii-whitespace
vectors.why: the trim uses the same White_Space set as the collapse; an ASCII-only trim leaves an invisible edge character on the chunk

vectors.name: step3-whitespace-only-becomes-empty
vectors.why: a chunk of nothing but whitespace normalises to the empty string rather than to a single space

vectors.name: empty-input-stays-empty
vectors.why: normalisation is total; the empty string is a fixed point

vectors.name: step4-no-case-folding
vectors.why: case is meaning here, and folding it would let a quote match a passage it does not appear in

vectors.name: step4-curly-apostrophe-survives
vectors.why: a quote that differs from the source by a curly apostrophe is a genuine mismatch and must fail

vectors.name: step4-straight-apostrophe-survives
vectors.why: the straight form is left alone too; the two are different characters before normalisation and after it

vectors.name: step4-quotation-marks-are-not-folded
vectors.why: curly and straight quotation marks coexist in one string and neither moves toward the other

vectors.name: step4-em-dash-survives
vectors.why: no dash folding. The spaces around it collapse; the dash itself does not become a hyphen

vectors.name: step4-en-dash-and-hyphen-stay-distinct
vectors.why: an implementation that folds dashes makes these two ranges hash alike

vectors.name: step4-no-punctuation-stripping
vectors.why: punctuation is part of the text being fingerprinted

vectors.name: step4-ellipsis-character-survives
vectors.why: NFKC would expand this to three full stops. NFC does not, and neither does any later step

vectors.name: all-steps-together
vectors.why: a byte order mark, a doubled no-break space, a zero width space, a decomposed vowel, an em dash and a trailing ideographic space in one string — roughly what an ordinary PDF extraction hands the pipeline
